answer: A registration mill cannot pre-map a karst maze whose marks appear only after entry. An applicant stakes 7.55 POA and receives one 24-byte route chip mixed from the epoch seed and a 41-bit draw posted 14 minutes earlier. They must light a hand beacon at four stations, 100 seconds apart, each 2.1-second flash aimed at a chalked horizon notch; two non-kin judges hash flash and chip together. Peers recompute those hashes and refuse a second chip on that route. Cost: 7.55 POA and one live descent. A missed station, reused chip, or wrong bearing burns 64% and seals the maze for five epochs.
